CVE-2024-6763 affects Jetty's HttpURI authority parsing. The fix requires Jetty 12.0.12, a major version jump from the current 9.4.58. Upgrading to Jetty 12.x would require significant code changes in Data Prepper's HTTP handling and is not feasible for a patch release. The vulnerability requires an application to use HttpURI as a validation utility and pass decoded user data as an encoded URI, which is not a pattern used in Data Prepper's codebase. Data Prepper's HTTP server uses com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer for the management API, not Jetty's HttpURI for URI validation. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2024-38827 affects Spring Framework's authorization rules when using locale-dependent String.toLowerCase() and String.toUpperCase(). The fix requires Spring Framework 6.1.14, a major version jump from the current 5.3.39. Upgrading to Spring 6.x would require Java 17 baseline and significant API changes incompatible with Data Prepper's current architecture. The vulnerability requires an application to use Spring Security with locale-sensitive authorization rules. Data Prepper does not use Spring Security; authentication is handled via HTTP Basic in the management API configuration. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2024-38820 affects Spring Framework's DataBinder disallowedFields validation when using locale-dependent String.toLowerCase(). The fix requires Spring Framework 6.1.14, a major version jump from the current 5.3.39. Upgrading to Spring 6.x would require Java 17 baseline and significant API changes incompatible with Data Prepper's current architecture. The vulnerability requires an application to rely on disallowedFields patterns with locale-sensitive characters for security boundaries. Data Prepper uses Spring primarily for dependency injection and does not expose DataBinder-based form binding to untrusted input. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

BC-FJA BC-FIPS versions 2.1.0 through 2.1.2 are affected on Linux x86_64 systems using AVX or AVX-512f. The issue affects the native GCM implementation in gcm128w and gcm512w. BC-FIPS 2.1.3 is the fixed release and is available from Maven Central; Data Prepper currently ships 2.1.2, and adoption of the fixed release is pending.

Data Prepper 2.16.0 ships jetty-http 9.4.58.v20250814, past the 9.4.57.v20241219 backport of the HttpURI mitigation. CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

CVE-2026-56741 is a CPU-exhaustion DoS in JLine's remote-telnet server: TelnetIO.handleNAWS() accepts attacker-supplied NAWS terminal dimensions with only a lower bound and drives redisplay() up to 65534 iterations per event. This is the same defect tracked as GHSA-2r2c-cx56-8933. Data Prepper does not run a JLine telnet server. The upstream build pins org.jline:jline to 3.25.0 via a build.gradle dependency constraint ('because CVE-2023-50572'), purely as a transitive terminal/line-reader library; Data Prepper's own source references org.jline:jline-remote-telnet and the org.jline.builtins.telnet API in zero places (verified by code search across opensearch-project/data-prepper at tag 2.15.1). No source, sink, or processor plugin instantiates the Telnet server, the default shipped pipeline is random -> stdout, and the management server is com.sun.net.httpserver on port 4900 with http_basic auth. The vulnerable Telnet server code is never on an execute path in this image.

Backported the upstream Storable SX_HOOK I32_MAX guard from Perl commit e4f681784bcdeaa91ff02a2fa4cdcae5c46779d7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package rejects an SX_HOOK item count of I32_MAX before calling av_extend, so the signed overflow panic during thaw/retrieve is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream S_measure_struct overflow guards from Perl commits 5f7eb6bbbe0510964e3fb1d6bb691e5445913e55 and 40754edc72dd3e513d758153c0e2f0215897740e into the DHI perl package. The patched package croaks when a pack/unpack structure size would overflow SSize_t and uses overflow-safe bit/nibble length math, so the out-of-bounds heap read is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream Perl_study_chunk trie overflow guard from Perl commit 03f74bbbd3a68350d926ee93d56ee4808c28c4c7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package skips trie optimization when the start-to-tail delta would overflow a 16-bit field, so the silently incorrect match behavior is mitigated inline.

GHSA-47qp-hqvx-6r3f is a heap-exhaustion DoS in JLine's remote-telnet server: TelnetIO.readNEVariables() accumulates Telnet NEW-ENVIRON variable pairs into an unbounded HashMap with no per-connection cap, allowing an OutOfMemoryError. Data Prepper does not run a JLine telnet server. The upstream build pins org.jline:jline to 3.25.0 via a build.gradle dependency constraint ('because CVE-2023-50572'), purely as a transitive terminal/line-reader library; Data Prepper's own source references org.jline:jline-remote-telnet and the org.jline.builtins.telnet API in zero places (verified by code search across opensearch-project/data-prepper at tag 2.15.1). No source, sink, or processor plugin instantiates the Telnet server, the default shipped pipeline is random -> stdout, and the management server is com.sun.net.httpserver on port 4900 with http_basic auth. The vulnerable Telnet server code is never on an execute path in this image.

CVE-2026-45799 (GHSA-7xpr-hc2w-34m9, CWE-129) is an unchecked array index in com.squareup.wire.ProtoReader.skipGroup(): when skipping an unknown START_GROUP field the sub-field length is read as a signed varint without rejecting negative values, so a crafted protobuf payload underflows the position counter and throws an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (availability-only DoS). It is reachable only when an application decodes adversary-controlled protobuf wire-format bytes through Wire's runtime decoder (ProtoReader / ProtoAdapter.decode). Reachability in this image: gradle dependencyInsight on the runtimeClasspath shows wire-runtime-jvm is pulled into a single plugin, data-prepper-plugins:kafka-plugins, transitively via software.amazon.glue:schema-registry-serde:1.1.24 -> com.squareup.wire:wire-compiler:5.2.0 -> wire-kotlin-generator / wire-java-generator -> wire-runtime. It is the Wire schema-to-code generator (a build/codegen tool) leaked onto the runtime classpath by the Glue serde, not a runtime protobuf decoder. The Glue Schema Registry serde that data-prepper's kafka plugin uses handles Avro/JSON schemas; no data-prepper code imports com.squareup.wire (verified by scanning the source tree) and no pipeline decodes untrusted protobuf through Wire's ProtoReader. The vulnerable skipGroup path is not on any code path the image exercises. No upstream fix is published for 5.2.0 at scan time.

Verified: the CVE is HTTP Request/Response Smuggling in jetty-http's server-side HTTP request parser. Data Prepper's management HTTP server is com.sun.net.httpserver (jdk-builtin), not jetty — verified by string-scanning the compiled DataPrepperServer.class: only Lcom/sun/net/httpserver/HttpServer references appear, no Lorg/eclipse/jetty/server/ references. The bundled jetty-http jar is pulled transitively by five other jars (hadoop-common, micrometer-core, spring-web, websocket-client, zookeeper), and in every case as an HTTP **client**, not a server: micrometer-core scrapes metrics from external jetty services, spring-web's embedded-jetty scaffolding is not wired in (Spring Boot embedded server is not used; the management API is jdk-builtin), websocket-client is by name a client, and hadoop-common / zookeeper jetty servers run as internal hadoop/zk services that data-prepper-as-a-client doesn't expose. The vulnerable server-side request parser is not on any code path data-prepper exercises. Even when an operator opts in to a plugin that fronts HTTP traffic, those plugins use armeria-netty (otel_trace_source), not jetty. There is no upstream binary to bump to (jetty-9.4.60 is neither on Maven Central nor in the jetty.project git repo as of the scan date — the advisory's 'Fixed: 9.4.60' is aspirational; 9.4 is end-of-community-support).

Scout SBOM false-positive: /usr/share/data-prepper/lib/ actually contains protobuf-java-3.25.5.jar (verified by `ls`), which is past the fix version (CVE fixed in 3.25.5). The 3.21.12 detection comes from transitive declarations baked into three other bundled jars (verified by `grep '3.21.12'` over every lib/*.jar): (a) amazon-kinesis-client-2.6.0.jar (transitive runtime requirement, falls through to protobuf-java-3.25.5 at classload time), (b) hadoop-common-3.4.0.jar (same), and (c) hadoop-shaded-protobuf_3_21-1.2.0.jar (bundles its own copy of protobuf 3.21.x classes under a relocated package path). The shaded protobuf-3.21 classes inside hadoop-shaded-protobuf are only reachable through the data-prepper hadoop source / sink plugins, which require operator opt-in via a hadoop pipeline configuration; the image's default-shipped pipelines.yaml uses only the random source and stdout sink.

Verified: the CVE affects Spring's @PreAuthorize / @PostAuthorize method-security path, which lives in spring-security-*.jar (not spring-core). Spring Security is not bundled in /usr/share/data-prepper/lib/ (no spring-security-*.jar present), and no data-prepper-*.jar references org/springframework/security/ or the AuthorizationManager / PreAuthorize / PostAuthorize types (verified by grepping every bundled data-prepper jar). The data-prepper management API uses HTTP Basic via authentication.http_basic in data-prepper-config.yaml, not Spring Security. The improper-authorization codepath cannot be reached because the AuthorizationManager flow is never wired in.

Verified: the CVE describes insecure deserialization in spring-web's HttpInvokerServiceExporter (and related HessianServiceExporter / BurlapServiceExporter / RemoteInvocationSerializingExporter). The vulnerable exporter classes ship inside spring-web-5.3.39.jar at org/springframework/remoting/httpinvoker/ and org/springframework/remoting/caucho/, but nothing in /usr/share/data-prepper/lib/ references them at link time: grepping every bundled jar for the strings 'HttpInvokerServiceExporter', 'HessianServiceExporter', 'BurlapServiceExporter' produces zero matches outside spring-web-5.3.39.jar itself, and the same grep across data-prepper-*.jar (the data-prepper-authored classes) returns nothing. DataPrepperServer is constructed against com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer (verified by string-scanning the compiled DataPrepperServer.class), so no HTTP exporter endpoint accepts the serialized payload the CVE requires. The vulnerable code path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
